detail.longDescription: Let's say I have the function import numpy as np def foo(a: float | np.ndarray, b: float | np.ndarray, c: float | np.ndarray, d: float | np.ndarray) -> float | np.ndarray: return a * b + c * d It only returns a float when all input parameters are float . As soon as one of them is an array, an array is returned. How can I efficiently type hint that behavior? Using simple overloads I have to specify five variants. from typing import overload @overload def foo(a: float, b: float, c: float, d: float) -> float: ... @overload def foo(a: np.ndarray, b: float | np.ndarray, c: float | np.ndarray, d: float | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: ... @overload def foo(a: float | np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray, c: float | np.ndarray, d: float | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: ... @overload def foo(a: float | np.ndarray, b: float | np.ndarray, c: np.ndarray, d: float | np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: ... @overload def foo(a: float | np.ndarray, b: float | np.ndarray, c: float | np.ndarray, d: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray: ... which, besides being a hassle, is not very transparent. and the problem only gets worse for more input parameters, of course. Is there a way to tell the type checker that, unless the first overload is satisfied, the return type will always be an array?
